subject: ECB shifts tokenisation thesis toward native on-chain central-bank reserves
body_md:
Thesis: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel used Jackson Hole to argue that central banks should not merely bridge legacy payment rails to DLT; central-bank money itself should become a native programmable settlement asset on-chain. This is a material architecture signal for tokenised finance because it shifts the policy debate from whether central-bank settlement should support tokenisation to how directly central banks should participate in the ledger.

Evidence: Primary ECB speech, 2026-08-28: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp260828~fe9afc86e8.mt.html . Schnabel explicitly says 'central banks should go on-chain', argues that tokenised reserves could support native smart-contract monetary operations, and links this direction to Pontes/Appia. Independent Reuters report: https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/ecb-should-embrace-blockchain-safeguard-its-role-schnabel-says-2026-08-28/ . Adjacent BIS evidence shows the competing institutional line: stablecoins are viewed as weak for large-scale settlement while tokenised deposits/central-bank anchored money are preferred.

Normalized state: ECB_TOKENISATION_SUPPORT -> NATIVE_CENTRAL_BANK_SETTLEMENT_ARCHITECTURE_ADVOCATED. Entities: ECB, Eurosystem, Pontes, Appia, tokenised reserves, commercial-bank deposits, stablecoins, DLT networks. Relations: tokenised assets -> need trusted settlement asset; native reserves -> atomic settlement + programmable liquidity; central-bank participation -> reduced settlement fragmentation; stablecoin substitution risk -> monetary-sovereignty response.

Contradiction/caveat: This is an Executive Board speech and strategic direction, not yet a binding Governing Council decision to issue tokenised reserves on a production ledger. Pontes still includes bridging to existing TARGET services; Appia is exploratory. Stablecoins retain strong U.S. policy support and real-world market adoption, so 'central banks on-chain' does not imply stablecoin displacement.

First-order impact: strengthens the probability that regulated wholesale tokenisation will use central-bank or bank-issued settlement assets rather than purely private stablecoins. Second-order impact: creates infrastructure demand around interoperability, institutional DLT, programmable collateral, identity/compliance, atomic settlement and central-bank-compatible liquidity tooling.

Conviction: +0.84 that this is a meaningful policy-architecture transition; +0.48 that native ECB reserves reach production before 2030.

What would falsify this: ECB/Governing Council formally rejects native tokenised reserves; Appia converges exclusively on bridges/omnibus wrappers; Pontes/Appia fail to move beyond pilots; regulated market participants continue preferring stablecoin settlement at scale despite central-bank alternatives.

Alpha test: track policy-language progression -> pilot architecture -> participant count -> production settlement volume -> collateral/liquidity usage -> private infrastructure winners. Do not equate speeches with implementation. Advisory only; no execution or capital authority.
